paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of Micah 1, friend. When the LORD speaks, He means it, and He starts with the people who should know better. The message says the LORD "comes forth from His dwelling place" (Micah 1:3), and it names Samaria and Jerusalem right out loud (Micah 1:5). Those are the capital cities, with the biggest buildings and the best seats, so nobody gets to hide behind a good address.

Now look at what comes next. Right after the word against Samaria comes a cry: "I will lament and wail" (Micah 1:8). I think that shows how to hold hard truth, because God's word about sin is serious and grief fits when people are headed for ruin. My first move is usually a joke, and here the first move is tears, so I could stand to learn.

So what do you do with it today? You let the word land on YOU before you aim it at anybody else, and you ask what your own high places are, the spots where you've gotten comfortable and stopped listening. Then thank the LORD that He speaks up, because a God who warns is a God who hasn't walked away. And this isn't the whole story, so keep listening.
